review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

8:1.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ καθεξῆς καὶ αὐτὸς διώδευεν κατὰ πόλιν καὶ κώμην κηρύσσων καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ οἱ δώδεκα σὺν αὐτῷ,
8:1.targetText: Soon afterward, Jesus traveled from one town and village to another, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with Him,

groups.note: ἐν τῷ καθεξῆς ("in the following time") is rendered Soon afterward.
The emphatic pronoun αὐτός ("he") is rendered by the name.
Distributive κατά ("town by town") is rendered from one … to another.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative frame Καὶ ἐγένετο ("and it came about") untranslated.
The καί that follows ἐγένετο is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The καί is not expressed; BSB starts a new sentence.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; the Greek has none here.

8:2.sourceText: καὶ γυναῖκές τινες αἳ ἦσαν τεθεραπευμέναι ἀπὸ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν καὶ ἀσθενειῶν, Μαρία ἡ καλουμένη Μαγδαληνή, ἀφ’ ἧς δαιμόνια ἑπτὰ ἐξεληλύθει,
8:2.targetText: as well as some women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,

groups.note: ἡ καλουμένη ("the one called") is rendered called.

8:3.sourceText: καὶ Ἰωάνα γυνὴ Χουζᾶ ἐπιτρόπου Ἡρῴδου καὶ Σουσάννα καὶ ἕτεραι πολλαί, αἵτινες διηκόνουν αὐτοῖς ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐταῖς.
8:3.targetText: Joanna the wife of Herod’s household manager Chuza, Susanna, and many others. These women were ministering to them out of their own means.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The genitive Χουζᾶ ("of Chuza") supplies of; ἐπιτρόπου Ἡρῴδου stands in apposition.
The relative αἵτινες ("who") begins a new English sentence as These women.
τὰ ὑπάρχοντα ("the things belonging") is rendered means.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB lists the names with commas, so these καί have no separate English word.

8:4.sourceText: Συνιόντος δὲ ὄχλου πολλοῦ καὶ τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ἐπιπορευομένων πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν διὰ παραβολῆς
8:4.targetText: While a large crowd was gathering and people were coming to Jesus from town after town, He told them this parable:

groups.note: The genitive absolute Συνιόντος … ὄχλου supplies the While-clause.
τῶν … ἐπιπορευομένων ("those journeying") is rendered people were coming.
Distributive κατὰ πόλιν ("town by town") is rendered from town after town.
The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered with the name Jesus.
διὰ παραβολῆς ("by a parable") is rendered as the object of told.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed; While belongs to the genitive absolute.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the hearers; εἶπεν has no written object.
English points ahead to the parable; the Greek has no demonstrative.

8:5.sourceText: Ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπεῖραι τὸν σπόρον αὐτοῦ. καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ὃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ κατεπατήθη, καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατέφαγεν αὐτό.
8:5.targetText: “A farmer went out to sow his seed. And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, where it was trampled, and the birds of the air devoured it.

groups.note: ὁ σπείρων ("the one sowing") is rendered A farmer.
τοῦ with the infinitive expresses purpose, "to sow".
ἐν τῷ with the infinitive is a temporal "as".
BSB turns "and it was trampled" into a where-clause, so this καί is rendered where.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The first member of the partition is expressed without a separate μέν word.

8:6.sourceText: καὶ ἕτερον κατέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν, καὶ φυὲν ἐξηράνθη διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ἰκμάδα.
8:6.targetText: Some fell on rocky ground, and when it came up, the seedlings withered because they had no moisture.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The article of the infinitive (διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν) has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the understood subject; ἐξηράνθη has only a verb ending.

8:7.sourceText: καὶ ἕτερον ἔπεσεν ἐν μέσῳ τῶν ἀκανθῶν, καὶ συνφυεῖσαι αἱ ἄκανθαι ἀπέπνιξαν αὐτό.
8:7.targetText: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up with it and choked the seedlings.

groups.note: ἐν μέσῳ ("in the midst of") is rendered among.
N1904 spells συνφυεῖσαι, the unassimilated form of συμφυεῖσαι; it is the same verb, "growing up together".
The repeated noun αἱ ἄκανθαι ("the thorns") is rendered by the relative which.
The pronoun αὐτό ("it", the seed) is rendered by its referent.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The καί is not expressed; English recasts the thorns clause as a relative clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the companion of the growing; the Greek has no pronoun.
English joins the participle συνφυεῖσαι (grew up with) to the main verb; the Greek has no conjunction here.

8:8.sourceText: καὶ ἕτερον ἔπεσεν εἰς τὴν γῆν τὴν ἀγαθήν, καὶ φυὲν ἐποίησεν καρπὸν ἑκατονταπλασίονα. ταῦτα λέγων ἐφώνει Ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.
8:8.targetText: Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprang up and produced a crop—a hundredfold.”  As Jesus said this, He called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

groups.note: BSB turns this καί into where, as in 8:5.
The participle λέγων supplies the As-clause.
ὁ ἔχων ("the one having") is rendered He who has.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle φυέν (sprang up) to the main verb; the Greek has no conjunction here.
English names the speaker; the Greek has only the participle.

8:9.sourceText: Ἐπηρώτων δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ τίς αὕτη εἴη ἡ παραβολή.
8:9.targetText: Then His disciples asked Him what this parable meant.

groups.note: εἴη ("might be") is rendered meant.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:10.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ, τοῖς δὲ λοιποῖς ἐν παραβολαῖς, ἵνα βλέποντες μὴ βλέπωσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες μὴ συνιῶσιν.
8:10.targetText: He replied, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to others I speak in parables, so that,  ‘though seeing, they may not see; though hearing, they may not understand.’

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.
The infinitive γνῶναι ("to know") is rendered with the noun knowledge.
The object of γνῶναι becomes the complement of English knowledge.
τοῖς λοιποῖς ("the rest") is rendered to others.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The καί is not expressed; English uses a semicolon.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; the Greek leaves it understood.

8:11.sourceText: ἔστιν δὲ αὕτη ἡ παραβολή. ὁ σπόρος ἐστὶν ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ.
8:11.targetText: Now this is the meaning of the parable: The seed is the word of God.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English spells out the explanation as the parable's meaning; the Greek says "this is the parable".

8:12.sourceText: οἱ δὲ παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν εἰσιν οἱ ἀκούσαντες, εἶτα ἔρχεται ὁ διάβολος καὶ αἴρει τὸν λόγον ἀπὸ τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν, ἵνα μὴ πιστεύσαντες σωθῶσιν.
8:12.targetText: The seeds along the path are those who hear, but the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.

groups.note: The article οἱ ("those") is rendered by its referent, the seeds.
οἱ ἀκούσαντες ("those who heard") is rendered those who hear.
εἶτα ("then") is rendered but.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle πιστεύσαντες (believe) to the main verb; the Greek has no conjunction here.

8:13.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἐπὶ τῆς πέτρας οἳ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν μετὰ χαρᾶς δέχονται τὸν λόγον, καὶ οὗτοι ῥίζαν οὐκ ἔχουσιν, οἳ πρὸς καιρὸν πιστεύουσιν καὶ ἐν καιρῷ πειρασμοῦ ἀφίστανται.
8:13.targetText: The seeds on rocky ground are those who hear the word and receive it with joy, but they have no root. They believe for a season, but in the time of testing, they fall away.

groups.note: The article οἱ ("those") is rendered by its referent, the seeds.
τὸν λόγον, the object of δέχονται, is rendered as the object of hear and repeated as it.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB recasts the ὅταν ("when") clause as a main clause joined by and.

English joins hear and receive; the Greek has a ὅταν clause, not a conjunction.

8:14.sourceText: τὸ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας πεσόν, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἀκούσαντες, καὶ ὑπὸ μεριμνῶν καὶ πλούτου καὶ ἡδονῶν τοῦ βίου πορευόμενοι συνπνίγονται καὶ οὐ τελεσφοροῦσιν.
8:14.targetText: The seeds that fell among the thorns are those who hear, but as they go on their way, they are choked by the worries, riches, and pleasures of this life, and their fruit does not mature.

groups.note: τὸ … πεσόν ("that which fell") is rendered The seeds that fell.
οἱ ἀκούσαντες ("those who heard") is rendered those who hear.

targetPhrases.text: as they go on their way

groups.note: N1904 spells συνπνίγονται, the unassimilated form of συμπνίγονται; it is the same verb.
τελεσφοροῦσιν ("they bring to maturity") is rendered their fruit does mature.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The resumptive οὗτοι ("these") is not repeated in English.
BSB lists the first two items with a comma, so this καί has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies this to mark the present life; the Greek has no demonstrative.

8:15.sourceText: τὸ δὲ ἐν τῇ καλῇ γῇ, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἵτινες ἐν καρδίᾳ καλῇ καὶ ἀγαθῇ ἀκούσαντες τὸν λόγον κατέχουσιν καὶ καρποφοροῦσιν ἐν ὑπομονῇ.
8:15.targetText: But the seeds on good soil are those with a noble and good heart, who hear the word, cling to it, and by persevering produce a crop.

groups.note: The article τό ("that") is rendered by its referent, the seeds.
The demonstrative οὗτοι ("these") is rendered those.
τὸν λόγον is the object of both hear and cling to; English repeats it as it.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:16.sourceText: Οὐδεὶς δὲ λύχνον ἅψας καλύπτει αὐτὸν σκεύει ἢ ὑποκάτω κλίνης τίθησιν, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ λυχνίας τίθησιν, ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι βλέπωσιν τὸ φῶς.
8:16.targetText: No one lights a lamp and covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.

groups.note: οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι ("the ones entering") is rendered those who enter.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἅψας (lights) to the main verb; the Greek has no conjunction here.
English repeats the object; τίθησιν has no written object.
English repeats the object; τίθησιν has no written object.

8:17.sourceText: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ φανερὸν γενήσεται, οὐδὲ ἀπόκρυφον ὃ οὐ μὴ γνωσθῇ καὶ εἰς φανερὸν ἔλθῃ.
8:17.targetText: For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be made known and brought to light.

groups.note: οὐ … κρυπτόν ("not … hidden") is rendered nothing hidden.
οὐ μή is an emphatic negative.

8:18.sourceText: βλέπετε οὖν πῶς ἀκούετε· ὃς ἂν γὰρ ἔχῃ, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ, καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ ἔχῃ, καὶ ὃ δοκεῖ ἔχειν ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.
8:18.targetText: Pay attention, therefore, to how you listen. Whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.”

unmappedSource.reason: The connective γάρ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The dative αὐτῷ ("to him") is expressed by making whoever the subject of the English passive.

8:19.sourceText: Παρεγένετο δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύναντο συντυχεῖν αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον.
8:19.targetText: Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came to see Him, but they were unable to reach Him because of the crowd.

groups.note: πρὸς αὐτόν ("to Him") is rendered came to see Him.
αὐτοῦ ("His") is rendered by the name Jesus.
οὐκ ἠδύναντο ("were not able") is rendered were unable.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:20.sourceText: ἀπηγγέλη δὲ αὐτῷ Ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἑστήκασιν ἔξω ἰδεῖν θέλοντές σε.
8:20.targetText: He was told, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see You.”

groups.note: The dative αὐτῷ ("to Him") becomes the subject of the English passive.
σου after each noun is rendered once, by Your.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

8:21.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Μήτηρ μου καὶ ἀδελφοί μου οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀκούοντες καὶ ποιοῦντες.
8:21.targetText: But He replied, “My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out.”

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.
ἀποκριθεὶς … εἶπεν ("answering, said") is rendered replied.
μου after each noun is rendered once, by My.
οἱ … ἀκούοντες ("the ones hearing") is rendered who hear.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the addressees πρὸς αὐτούς ("to them") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:22.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἐνέβη εἰς πλοῖον καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς λίμνης· καὶ ἀνήχθησαν.
8:22.targetText: One day Jesus said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” So He got into a boat with them and set out.

groups.note: ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν ("on one of the days") is rendered One day.
καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ("and His disciples") is rendered with them.

8:23.sourceText: πλεόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἀφύπνωσεν. καὶ κατέβη λαῖλαψ ἀνέμου εἰς τὴν λίμνην, καὶ συνεπληροῦντο καὶ ἐκινδύνευον.

groups.note: The genitive absolute πλεόντων αὐτῶν supplies the As-clause.

8:24.sourceText: προσελθόντες δὲ διήγειραν αὐτὸν λέγοντες Ἐπιστάτα ἐπιστάτα, ἀπολλύμεθα. ὁ δὲ διεγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ ἀνέμῳ καὶ τῷ κλύδωνι τοῦ ὕδατος· καὶ ἐπαύσαντο, καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη.

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he; BSB names Jesus.

8:25.targetText: “Where is your faith?” He asked.  Frightened and amazed, they asked one another, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!”

groups.note: πρὸς ἀλλήλους ("to one another") is rendered as the object of asked.

8:26.sourceText: Καὶ κατέπλευσαν εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γερασηνῶν, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἀντιπέρα τῆς Γαλιλαίας.
8:26.targetText: Then they sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, across the lake from Galilee.

groups.note: ἀντιπέρα ("opposite") is rendered across … from.

8:27.sourceText: ἐξελθόντι δὲ αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ὑπήντησεν ἀνήρ τις ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ἔχων δαιμόνια, καὶ χρόνῳ ἱκανῷ οὐκ ἐνεδύσατο ἱμάτιον, καὶ ἐν οἰκίᾳ οὐκ ἔμενεν ἀλλ’ ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν.
8:27.targetText: When Jesus stepped ashore, He was met by a demon-possessed man from the town. For a long time this man had not worn clothing or lived in a house, but he stayed in the tombs.

groups.note: The participle ἐξελθόντι is rendered as a When-clause.
αὐτῷ is both the one stepping ashore and the one met, rendered Jesus and He.
ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ("onto the land") is rendered ashore.

8:28.sourceText: ἰδὼν δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀνακράξας προσέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ εἶπεν Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Υἱὲ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου; δέομαί σου, μή με βασανίσῃς.
8:28.targetText: When the man saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before Him, shouting in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You not to torture me!”

8:29.sourceText: παρήγγελλεν γὰρ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. πολλοῖς γὰρ χρόνοις συνηρπάκει αὐτόν, καὶ ἐδεσμεύετο ἁλύσεσιν καὶ πέδαις φυλασσόμενος, καὶ διαρήσσων τὰ δεσμὰ ἠλαύνετο ἀπὸ τοῦ δαιμονίου εἰς τὰς ἐρήμους.
8:29.targetText: For Jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him, and though he was bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and been driven by the demon into solitary places.

groups.note: BSB turns the clauses joined by this καί into "though he was bound …, he had broken …".
N1904 spells διαρήσσων with one ρ; it is the same verb, διαρρήσσω ("break apart").
ἀπό with the passive ἠλαύνετο marks the demon as the agent, by; BSB's Greek text may have a different preposition here.
